# Sapwood

> Managing a Heartwood ESP32 hardware signer normally means a serial terminal
> or a cloud dashboard. Sapwood is a browser-based management UI: connect over
> USB with the Web Serial API, or manage remotely over authenticated Nostr
> relays once the device is online.

Sapwood is for anyone running a Heartwood signer who wants a UI for
identities, connected apps, WiFi, firmware and backups without a server or
cloud account in the loop. Local USB management uses the Web Serial API
directly; remote management sends authenticated, encrypted events over Nostr
relays to the device's outbound WiFi connection, so there is no inbound port
and no management server to trust. It is a static SPA (Svelte 5), and the
same functionality is also available as a cross-platform CLI.

## Getting started

```
git clone https://github.com/forgesworn/sapwood.git
cd sapwood
npm install
npm run dev       # dev server at localhost:5173
```

Or visit the hosted build in Chrome or Edge, plug in a Heartwood device, and
click Connect USB. For the CLI: `npm run build:cli && npm link`, then run
`sapwood device`.

## Key concepts

- Frame protocol: USB traffic is a TypeScript port of the Rust frame format in
  heartwood-common (`src/lib/frame.ts`): `[0x48 0x57] [type_u8] [length_u16_be]
  [payload...] [crc32_be32]`.
- Two transports, one state store: USB (Web Serial) and remote (Nostr relays)
  both feed the same reactive device state, so UI components do not know
  which transport is active.
- Physical button confirmation gates every destructive or secret-revealing
  operation on the device (factory reset, OTA, backup export/import,
  provisioning). A compromised browser tab cannot act without it.
- Named identities: the signer derives child identities from a master it
  already holds (`DERIVE_IDENTITY`), so no secret needs to enter the browser.
- Exact client policies: connected apps are scoped to specific NIP-46 methods
  and event kinds; unlisted methods and kinds fail closed.

## API surface

Frame types are defined in `src/lib/frame.ts` (`FrameType`), including
provisioning (`PROVISION_LIST`, `PROVISION_LIST_RESPONSE`), identity
derivation (`DERIVE_IDENTITY`, `DERIVE_IDENTITY_RESPONSE`), remote signing
(`ENCRYPTED_REQUEST`, `SIGN_ENVELOPE_RESPONSE`), connected-app management
(`CONNSLOT_LIST`, `CONNSLOT_REVOKE` and related `CONNSLOT_*` frames), OTA
firmware update (`OTA_BEGIN`/`OTA_CHUNK`/`OTA_FINISH`/`OTA_STATUS`), and
backup/restore (`BACKUP_EXPORT_REQUEST`/`BACKUP_EXPORT_RESPONSE`,
`BACKUP_IMPORT_REQUEST`/`BACKUP_IMPORT_RESPONSE`).

The CLI (`cli/commands.ts`) exposes the same operations as subcommands:
`device`, `identities`, `identities remove`, `derive`, `apps`,
`apps revoke`, `logs`, `firmware update`, `key backup`, `operator new`,
`operator restore`, `backup export`, `backup import`. All support `--json`.
